answer: Each identity must show one distinct circadian rhythm: 30 days of activity logs with a single six-to-nine-hour sleep gap at consistent local times, like a lone island keeping its own hours in a quiet meadow. A farm operator running many fakes from one desk leaves either identical gaps or none at all, and the signal gives it away. Faking one rhythm costs about $60 in operator time; 100 distinct, consistent rhythms cost about $6,000 and get harder to keep apart every epoch.
